quote: Sorry. Just one other person, my husband.
stewart_read: The husband is identified as a co-owner on the title within the first minute, but he is never mentioned again — not at scheduling, not in the button-up. The appointment is booked with only Kim confirmed.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have assumed Kim would loop in her husband herself since he wasn't presented as a co-decision-maker objection; but the schema treats co-owner identification as a trigger regardless of whether it surfaces as an explicit objection.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly confirm the co-owner's attendance at booking: 'Since your husband's also on the title, let's get a time that works for both of you.' This appointment is booked structurally vulnerable to a no-show or a stalled close if the husband isn't present.

quote: off solar. And do you guys have, like, like, generators for the solar panels?
stewart_read: Customer's stated reason for solar (running a pool heater) plus an unprompted question about battery backup are two distinct signals of higher usage and specific product interest that the rep could have anchored on when setting up the appointment's value.
coaching_implication: Flag for the rep: when a customer volunteers a specific use case (pool heater) and asks about batteries unprompted, reflect it back ('so we'll want to size this so it covers the pool heater too') rather than filing it and moving to the next verify item — this creates curiosity and previews value for the specialist call.

quote: We have batteries that we might have generators. You can talk to the so I'm basically, I'm just building design, so you talk to the specialist.
stewart_read: The rep starts to answer the battery/generator question directly before catching himself and redirecting to the specialist — a partial scope-creep moment that self-corrects mid-sentence.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as strategic (a quick acknowledgment before redirecting) rather than a failure, since the redirect does happen within the same breath.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the redirect habit — it worked here — but tighten the opening so the rep doesn't start improvising specs at all before redirecting, per the universal escape hatch language.

quote: Not really sure how to find the yearly, but I found, like, just month.
stewart_read: This is portal-navigation friction on an at-home customer, not the mobile/away-from-home shopping_customer_protocol scenario. The rep repeats generic navigational guidance ('filter system') rather than pivoting to a verbal read-back of the monthly usage number the customer already found, which would have unblocked the call faster.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep didn't recognize the friction pattern in time to pivot. Strategic read is weak here — there's no evidence the rep was deliberately holding out for the photo for a specific reason beyond habit.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on a 2-minute pivot rule: when a customer states confusion navigating an online portal, accept a read-aloud number as a stopgap rather than repeating navigation instructions.

quote: It says it's two thousand three sixty.
stewart_read: The customer gives a usable annual kWh usage figure verbally, but the rep does not accept it as sufficient or use it as an anchor — he redirects back to needing the photo instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: Ion's design process may genuinely require the photo/graph rather than a verbal number, making the rep's insistence procedurally correct rather than a missed anchor.
coaching_implication: Even if the photo is required for design purposes, the rep could have acknowledged the number conversationally ('2,360 — okay, that gives me a sense of your usage') before redirecting to the photo, turning a procedural ask into a moment of engagement.

quote: Okay. I so you're in Richmond? That's your that's what you're assigned to? But you're not in Richmond?
stewart_read: The rep discovers a territory/team assignment mismatch live on the call and works through it transparently in front of the customer rather than hiding the uncertainty.
coaching_implication: This is a minor, fully-resolved operational hiccup (customer clarifies Chesterfield vs Richmond and the rep proceeds to book Monday) — not a coaching priority, but worth noting the rep handled the uncertainty transparently rather than fumbling silently.

quote: So I got you down for 09:30, on the twenty third, Monday.
stewart_read: The rep confirms day and time but never runs the full button-up: no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, and no text-follow-up promise beyond the earlier bill-collection text.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full button-up checklist even on short, cooperative calls — the missing no-driving/computer instruction and handshake are predictive of no-show risk per schema guidance.
